newsitem.title: FRANCE: French teenagers getting taste of alcohol earlier.
newsitem.headline: French teenagers getting taste of alcohol earlier.

text.p: French teenagers are getting a taste of wine, beer and spirits earlier than a decade ago in a country with one of the world's highest rates of alcohol consumption, a survey showed on Tuesday.

However consumption among male teenagers overall had been stable since 1985 despite a slide in consumption among adults of about one percent a year, according to the survey by the Institute of Scientific Research on Drink (IREB).

The survey found that the number of boys aged 13 and 14 who never drank had fallen to 63 percent in 1996 from 72 percent in 1985, while the number of teetotallers aged 15 and 16 fell to 30 percent from 44 percent in 1985.
Most drank only tiny amounts, the survey found.

Boys and young men aged 13-18 drank 20.3 alcoholic drinks a month last year, up from 19.9 in 1985, in a nation with famed wines ranging from Champagne to Burgundy. IREB said the gain was not statistically significant.
A wider survey with no comparisons with 1985 showed that girls and young women aged 13-20 drank an average of 13.6 glasses a month in 1996, far less than 28.9 for males.

"I think we haven't yet found efficient methods of prevention (of abuse)," said Jacques Weill, head of the IREB scientific committee. "The figures let us believe that what's been done up to now has not been very effective."
Consumption in France overall has declined steadily by about a third over the past three decades to 11.7 litres of pure alcohol a year per person, or about 80 glasses a month.
The fall has been in consumption of table wines -- beers, spirits and quality wines have been unaffected.

Weill said the solution to alcohol abuse among the young was widespread education both in schools and at home. He said that jacking up prices was also not a solution, saying it spurred smuggling and moonshine.
IREB's survey covered 997 people aged 13-20. IREB is funded by the French drinks industry. France limits ages for drinking in bars and cafes but children of any age can buy alcohol freely in shops.
